note: Researched from the club's Wikipedia article and the club's own website, then checked by Danny before it went live. Everything here is sourced, nothing invented.

story.title: The first shirt sponsors in England
story.text: In January 1976, under Derek Dougan, Kettering became the first English club to wear a sponsor on its shirts, carrying Kettering Tyres against Bath City on 24 January. The FA ordered the logo removed and threatened a £1,000 fine. Dougan tried shortening it to Kettering T and claimed the T stood for Town. The FA were not amused and it came off, but by June 1977 they had relented and allowed sponsors' logos of up to two and a half square inches. Every shirt in English football since owes something to that afternoon.

story.title: More FA Cup goals than anyone
story.text: Kettering have scored more goals in the FA Cup than any other club in the competition's history, which takes some doing for a club outside the Football League. The best of it came in 1988-89: Dartford in the first round, then Football League Bristol Rovers, then Halifax Town, before a 2-1 defeat at First Division Charlton Athletic in the fourth. The club got that far again in 2008-09.

story.title: One vote from the Football League
story.text: Four times between the wars the club applied to join the Football League and four times it was turned down, twice receiving a single vote. The closest they came was in the early 1960s, when they polled sixteen votes as the highest-ranked non-League club in the ballot, only five behind Fourth Division Workington. Automatic promotion did not exist yet, so that was the only door in, and it stayed shut.

story.title: Founder members of the national league
story.text: In 1979 Kettering were among the founder members of the Alliance Premier League, the first single national division at the top of non-League football and the direct ancestor of today's National League. They were runners-up in 1980-81 and again in 1988-89, losing the play-off final 4-2 to AFC Telford United after seeing off Harborough Town on penalties in the semi.

story.title: From Rockingham Road to Latimer Park
story.text: The club played at North Park, then Green Lane, before settling at Rockingham Road in 1897 and staying for over a century. In 2012 they were forced out and spent a season at Steel Park in Corby, moving to Burton Park Wanderers' ground at Latimer Park in Burton Latimer the year after. It is a long way from Rockingham Road, and plenty of supporters will tell you so.

story.title: Last season
story.text: Kettering reached the play-offs under Liam McDonald, finishing fourth having been close to the relegation places at the halfway point. The season ended with a 3-1 defeat to Real Bedford in the semi-final. McDonald stepped down on 6 August 2026, days before the new campaign started.

managers.note: Fifty three spells in charge since 1956, and six men have had the job more than once. Morell Maison managed it three times. Steve Gammon lasted longest, six years from 1965, which nobody has come close to since.

officials.note: One thing the club's own page has not caught up with: it still lists Liam McDonald as first team manager, and the club announced he stepped down on 6 August. Nick Green is shown here in the job he is actually doing. Everything else is as the club has it, including its spellings.
officials.boardNote: Fifteen roles across the boardroom and the day to day running of the club, chaired by the owner. Three board members stood down over the summer: Graham Starmer, Doug Brown and Rob McGreavey, which the club described as their own decision. Doug Brown still appears below on matchday media.

ground.name: Latimer Park
ground.address: Polwell Lane, Burton Latimer, Kettering, NN15 5PS
paragraphs: Latimer Park is not in Kettering. It sits in Burton Latimer, about two and a half miles south east of the town centre and a similar distance from where Rockingham Road used to be, which catches out plenty of first-time visitors. Set the postcode rather than the town.

The club has been here since 2013, sharing with Burton Park Wanderers, after being forced out of Rockingham Road in 2012 and spending a season at Steel Park in Corby. Rockingham Road had been home since 1897.
ground.note: No official capacity for Latimer Park is published anywhere we can find, so there is no figure here rather than a guess.
